title: Teacher contract renewals and recruitment planning for next year
description: A practical guide for Kenyan school principals on managing BOM-employed teacher contract renewals and planning recruitment for staffing gaps ahead of the new academic year.
body:
For BOM-employed teaching staff — a significant proportion of teaching capacity in many Kenyan schools, particularly for specific subjects or pathway needs — contract renewal and recruitment planning for the following year needs to happen well before the current year ends, not as an urgent scramble once the new year has already begun.

Reviewing contract status systematically

A simple audit of all BOM-employed staff contracts — expiry dates, renewal terms, any performance considerations relevant to the renewal decision — conducted in good time before the academic year ends, avoids the situation where a contract lapses without a clear decision having been made about renewal.

Basing renewal decisions on genuine performance evidence

Renewal decisions grounded in the kind of evidence discussed in our guide on meaningful teacher appraisal — actual classroom performance, student outcomes, professional conduct — are both fairer to the staff member and more defensible than decisions based on informal impression alone.

Identifying staffing gaps early

Enrolment projections, curriculum needs for the coming year (particularly CBE pathway-specific staffing requirements), and any known departures should be reviewed together to identify genuine staffing gaps before the new year begins, giving the school adequate time to recruit well rather than filling a gap reactively once term has already started.

Common staffing gap: Schools expanding their CBE pathway offerings, particularly adding or strengthening STEM pathway subjects, sometimes discover staffing gaps only once the new academic year's timetable is being built. Reviewing pathway staffing needs against current capacity in October, rather than in January, gives genuine recruitment lead time.

Running a genuine recruitment process

A recruitment process that is structured — clear job requirements, a genuine shortlisting process, structured interviews — attracts and identifies stronger candidates than an informal process based primarily on personal networks or convenience. This matters particularly for specialist subject areas where qualified candidates may be limited.

Onboarding planning, not just hiring

A new teacher hired for the following year benefits from the same structured onboarding approach covered in our guide on onboarding mid-year — a briefing pack, a mentor colleague, clear expectations — prepared in advance of their start date, not improvised once they arrive.

Communicating with the BOM throughout

Contract renewal and recruitment decisions for BOM-employed staff are ultimately BOM decisions, requiring the principal to bring clear recommendations, supported by evidence, to the BOM in good time for a considered decision — not a last-minute approval request that leaves little room for genuine governance input.
